speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance of the rash on your trunk and extremities, and tell me exactly when it started relative to your fever and other symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the rash on her body appear as a "slapped cheek" appearance, and is it spreading in a lacy, reticular pattern? I also need to know if she has been around anyone with similar symptoms recently.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical picture of a "slapped cheek" facial rash followed by a lacy, reticular rash on the trunk and extremities is classic for Erythema Infectiosum, also known as Fifth Disease. Given the typical presentation, I am confident in my assessment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
